doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The 1960s groups, Madison Avenue and film
title: Wide World of Music: hustling the jobs, TV burnout, and the advertising crowd
summary: He ran Wide World of Music with arranger Jimmy Cheatham, did all the hustling himself, started drinking martini lunches, and grew burned out repeating himself.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Up to here with what?

Well I got burned out. TV can ruin you man. TV can suck all your talent, take all your talent. You know, for anybody to last on TV is amazing in a sense because man it can really burn you out, you know. I got to the point man where I would pigeonhole things. I was just doing things for money, which I guess nothing’s wrong with that but you reach a point where you find yourself repeating yourself. I wouldn’t even listen to the radio or nothing because I didn’t want to be influenced by anything, you know. I want to be original, you know.

Let’s talk about the development of Wide World of Music. So the first thing you did was you realized you had an opportunity so you bring in a close partner, Jimmy Cheatham. So are you equal partners or is he working with you, working for you?
He’s sort of working with me. I did all the hustling. I did all the hustling.
Well that was what I was going to ask. So how do you start to develop your staff and how do you start to develop this business, just for any other entrepreneurs?

No, Jimmy was the only one -- you know, I did the composing, he did the arranging. And I went out and got the jobs, I went out and hustled the spots. I went out and, you know, hung out and did, you know -­
So you didn’t hire a publicist, you didn’t have a manager?
No, no, I did it all myself, man.
So you had to at least have an admin, somebody, a secretary?
No, I did it all myself, man.
Everything.
I did everything. I learned how to drink in the daytime, martinis at lunch. I had never drank before evening time.
Was it because that was part of the business, you meeting folks?

Three-martini lunch. You always had martinis at lunch. Advertising people is something else, man, you know. My whole lifestyle changed, man, I became -- I didn’t hang out with musicians, I hung out with producers, writers, and people like that, art directors.
Such as, do you remember -­

Well, you know, Jerry Schatzberg. Name some of the -- you know, I hung out with all the photographers, Bert Stern, people like that, writers like Don Stewart. He and I became very close. He won the Academy Award for Missing -- the writer. I just hung out with people, you know, in the advertising world.
But a different breed of animal.
Oh, man.
Different from the musician milieu.
Completely different, man, completely different. But they were my eyes to a whole lot of things, you know, different -- but they were different.
